BiblicalUsage: Tsama is thirst — the dry, urgent need for water, and for the God who gives it. Israel thirsted in the wilderness and murmured against Moses; Isaiah promises that when the poor and needy seek water and there is none, God will hear them; and Amos warns of a famine in the land, not of bread nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD. The psalmist's thirst was met with vinegar — a verse fulfilled when Christ was given vinegar on the cross.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe thirst is the truest picture of what a soul is without God — dry, urgent, and unable to help itself. My position is that God alone satisfies the thirst He put in us, and a thirst for His word is a worse famine than a thirst for water. I hold that He hears the thirsty who seek Him, and He will not let them go dry.
